To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a snake anticoagulant factor, X-bp, binds to the Ca2+-binding Gla domain of blood coactivator factor X and that the antico-agulant activity is based on the burial of the two Ca2+-binding patches of the Gli domain.

the crystal structure of the complex of the Gla-domain of blood coagulant factor X with the snake venom protein X-bp reveals that the Gla-domain is a potential new target for anticoagulant drug design and provides a model for a membrane-bound factor X.
X-bp is a novel inhibitor of factor Xa and factor Xa is a new target of X-bp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying the biological function of blood coagulant factors.
elucidating the molecular mechanism of anticoagulation by X-bp, and the results are expected to provide the basis for the design of novel anticoagulant agents.
the structure of the complex of X-bp and the Gla domain and the mechanism of anticoagulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
X-bp is the first protein that has been shown to specifically bind to the Gla-domain peptide of factor X and that the Gla-domain binding site is the membrane-binding site of factor X.

the Gla domain and the γ-carboxy-glutamic acid residues of the Gla domains of blood coagulant proteins are essential for the membrane binding of the proteins and that this binding is inhibited by the anticoagulant X-bp.
the anticoagonulant activity of X-bp is based on the inhibition of membrane binding of the Gla domains of factor X.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of the Gla-Xbp complex is the first example of the structural basis for the membrane-bound model of blood coagulant factor and the first example for anticoagulant mechanism based on the fact of membrane binding.
X-bp is a new type of anticoagulation factor, which acts by binding to the Gla region of factor X and blocking its binding to phospholipid membranes.
the Gla domain is a novel target of antico-agulant drug development, and the X-bp-Gla domain complex provides a structural basis for designing such drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gla domain is an ideal drug target because of its high affinity and specificity for membranes and because it is a key player in the coagulation cascade.
X-bp is a novel anticoagulant drug candidate that can be used for the treatment of thrombotic disorders.
the structure provides a basis for understanding the mechanism of the interaction of X-bp with the Gla domains of factors X and IX and the design of new anticoagulant agents.
